newsitem.title: USA: Case sees solid customer demand.
newsitem.headline: Case sees solid customer demand.

text.p: Case Corp said Thursday that solid customer demand and strong underlying economic fundamentals make the outlook positive for its agricultural and construction equipment markets.
"Consistent with 1996, Case anticipates that unit production and wholesale sales will be at or below retail demand for all of 1997," the company said in a release.

The heavy equipment maker also said that in the 1997 first quarter, preparation for significant new product introductions will result in lower production of certain products than in the first quarter of 1996, but no adverse impact on full-year production schedules is expected.
In the agricultural sector, commodity prices are expected to remain favorable as worldwide demand for grains and other agricultural products is expected to continue to grow, Case said.

The construction equipment sector is gaining strength in the United Kingdom and Australia, and is maintaining favorable levels in North America. Housing starts are generally increasing in these markets, Case said.
The company said it believes France and Germany could continue to experience significant weakness until economic growth and construction spending resume.
In Latin America, economic conditions in Brazil have greatly improved and retail sales of construction equipment are expected to be strong, it said.
Case today reported higher fourth quarter earning.
